question: Which local, maintainable tools support a premium interactive Ashvane observatory and an evidence-driven maintenance supervisor?

claims.statement: Three.js provides a bloom postprocessing pass and raycasting for selectable 3D objects; this establishes features, not measured Ashvane performance.
Three.js documentation recommends rendering on demand for views that change only with data or interaction, and discusses responsive GPU resolution costs.
Rive supports distinct WebGL2 and Canvas runtime choices; its documentation advises measuring against actual content rather than treating either as universally faster.
React Flow and Cytoscape provide interactive graph tooling; adopting React Flow into the existing vanilla desktop would add a framework boundary.
The official MCP Registry supports discovery and MCP Inspector supports testing server tools; discovery is distinct from granting runtime access.
LangGraph documents checkpoints and stores as different forms of persisted agent state; memory alone is not proof of model training.
Playwright supports screenshot comparison and mobile emulation; its MCP project also documents structured browser interaction.
Space Grotesk and IBM Plex repositories publish their font families under the SIL Open Font License; bundled files retain the license text.
Self-Refine and Reflexion investigate output refinement and feedback memory without making automatic weight changes a prerequisite; those papers do not establish Ashvane model quality.
The Nature model-collapse study reports degradation under indiscriminate recursive generated-data training; generated examples require independent evaluation before training claims.
